topic: Binomial Nomenclature and Scientific Naming Rules
title: One Fish, Three Names? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Bangude in Kannada, Ayla in Malayalam, Bangda in Marathi: three names for the very same fish. Diya hears all three at one fish stall and asks which name a scientist uses. Scientists everywhere call it Rastrelliger kanagurta.

You will see why common names fail, why identification comes before naming, and how Carolus Linnaeus gave every species a two-word name. A labelled diagram takes Mangifera indica Linn. apart (generic name, specific epithet, author, italics), then names run through four rule gates: Latin, two parts, capital and small letters, italics or separate underlines. Meet ICBN and ICZN, compare common and scientific names, fix three badly written names, then the exam trap about the species name, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 8 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
